scope: Correct the public labels and tabletop refinement selection for the long egocentric silver five-finger RV2V demo
summary: Publication revision 2 labels both result panels PhiAgent and promotes the requested localized 19-25-second tabletop refinement instead of the later full-timeline background-restoration result.
evidence: The corrected browser comparisons decode completely as H.264 High, yuv420p, 1280x360, 24 FPS with exact 862- and 964-frame timelines.

The tabletop browser comparison SHA-256 is 34c0b6938d52a13b6314f77a4f4525f5360768a4e3bff7a061516606ff7651da and is derived from the localized refined lossless artifact with SHA-256 490ded67e0693ff33665665a0c8bf54d677278a129007b8bf9ea1df92715ca33.

The localized tabletop audit records a 19-25-second core, 18.5-25.5-second transition context, exact direct-candidate pixels outside the transition window, and exact safe source pixels within the core.

The device/cable browser comparison SHA-256 is b3b8f01d7a509e104fc58968f89685106c3bcf8d88e71d8633e5f96797bb7062; its visual result is unchanged from selected seed 73 apart from the corrected baked label.
lessons: A public-media selector must distinguish a requested localized repair from a later full-timeline experimental refinement even when both derive from the same selected RV2V seed.
Product-facing comparison labels should name PhiAgent rather than exposing an internal RV2V processing label.
Versioned correction media preserve the earlier evidence while allowing the demo page to promote the user-selected result.
limitations: This record validates the correction package before the follow-up main-branch push and Pages deployment.
The localized refinement remains a camera-frame SAM2 source-state projection, not evidence of robot kinematics or physical execution.
Thin cables and robot fingers in the device clip remain vulnerable to local sticking, deformation, or flicker.
next_actions: Push the correction commit to main and verify the GitHub Pages workflow.
Verify the public revision-2 homepage, comparison videos, posters, and evaluation hashes.
